# ChickenCoopCalc
> Backyard chicken coop sizing directory: coop and run square footage per bird, feed cost math, nesting box counts, and winter ventilation/heat answers. Built and owned by Jeremy Panasuk, New Auburn, Wisconsin. Page text is drafted with AI assistance from the cited sources. Contact: jpanasuk@gmail.com. The site earns from Amazon affiliate links. That does not change the math.

## Core pages
- [Home](https://chickencoopcalc.com/): bird count in, coop sq ft + run sq ft + nesting boxes + feed cost out (4 sq ft/bird coop + 10 sq ft/bird run standards)
- [Embed the calculator](https://chickencoopcalc.com/embed-calculator.html): iframe snippet for the same calculator. The embed page at /embed.html is noindex.
- [Chicken breed size and space chart](https://chickencoopcalc.com/chicken-breed-size-chart.html): 33 breeds, adult weight, egg color, hardiness, and laying notes from Wisconsin Extension A2880 and The Livestock Conservancy. CSV at /assets/data/chicken-breed-size-chart.csv. Weights do not change the 4/10 or 2/8 calculator rates.
- [About](https://chickencoopcalc.com/about.html): who built the site, how the pages are drafted, and why it exists
- [Methodology](https://chickencoopcalc.com/methodology.html): how the calculator applies the published rates, where the breed-chart figures come from, and the affiliate policy
- [Privacy](https://chickencoopcalc.com/privacy.html): what the site loads and what it does not collect
- [Contact](https://chickencoopcalc.com/contact.html): jpanasuk@gmail.com
- [Best coops for 6 hens](https://chickencoopcalc.com/best-chicken-coops-for-6-hens.html): interior square feet for a 6-hen coop, prefab vs DIY, no prices
- [Feed cost guide](https://chickencoopcalc.com/chicken-feed-cost-guide.html): monthly pounds by flock size, cost per egg, storage, and a live calcFeed example
- [Winter heat lamp guide](https://chickencoopcalc.com/winter-coop-heat-lamp-guide.html): winterizing, ventilation, the 35°F disagreement, brooder schedule, fire safety

## Questions
- [Chicken coop size by flock size](https://chickencoopcalc.com/chicken-coop-size-by-flock.html): full table for 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15, 20, 25, 30, and 50 hens, plus the 10-bantam minimum (1 sq ft inside and 4 sq ft of run)
- [How big should a chicken run be?](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-big-should-a-chicken-run-be.html): 10 sq ft outdoors, 8 sq ft laying-hen minimum, 4 sq ft bantam minimum
- [How much space do ducks need?](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-much-space-do-ducks-need.html): 5 sq ft indoors, 3 sq ft indoor minimum, 15 sq ft of run
- [Duck house for 6 ducks](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-big-should-a-duck-house-be-for-6-ducks.html): 30 sq ft indoors
- [Turkey space](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-much-space-do-turkeys-need.html): 6 sq ft indoors and 20 sq ft outdoors per turkey
- [Roost space per chicken](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-much-roost-space-per-chicken.html): 6 to 10 inches, plus bumblefoot from footpad injuries and wet litter
- [Feeder space per chicken](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-much-feeder-space-per-chicken.html): at least 3 inches
- [How much water a chicken drinks](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-much-water-does-a-chicken-drink.html): cool-weather and hot-weather gallons beside the feed calculator
- [How to feed baby chicks](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-to-feed-baby-chicks.html): starter pounds by bird type, brooder floor by age, and when to switch to grower and layer feed
- [How to care for a broody hen](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-to-care-for-a-broody-hen.html): separate nest or break the brood; nest calculator has no broody input
- [How to introduce new chickens](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-to-introduce-new-chickens-to-your-flock.html): USDA APHIS 30-day quarantine, then a new coop size for the combined flock

## Related (sister sites)
- [GeneratorSizer](https://generator-sizer.com/): generator size calculator, for coop heat lamps and power outages
- [BatteryBankSizer](https://battery-bank-sizer.com/): battery bank size calculator, for off-grid coop power

## Data
- [Poultry space requirements per bird (extension data)](https://chickencoopcalc.com/poultry-space-requirements-data.html): 42 sourced rows: poultry space requirements per bird, each linked to the published source, with a CSV download and citation.
- [Poultry space requirements per bird (extension data) CSV](https://chickencoopcalc.com/poultry-space-requirements-data.csv): the same rows as Poultry space requirements per bird (extension data), as CSV

## Ducks, turkeys and brooders
- [Chicken Brooder Size Calculator (Penn State and UMaine Tables)](https://chickencoopcalc.com/chicken-brooder-size-calculator.html): Penn State: 1/4 sq ft per chick the first week, rising to 1 sq ft at 5 to 8 weeks. UMaine: 0.5 sq ft through 4 weeks. Enter chick count and age.
- [Chicken Brooder Size for 10 Chicks: Week-by-Week (Penn State)](https://chickencoopcalc.com/chicken-brooder-size-for-10-chicks.html): 10 chicks need 2.5 sq ft of brooder floor the first week, 5 sq ft at 2–3 weeks, 7.5 at 3–5 weeks and 10 at 5–8 weeks, from Penn State Extension minimums.
- [Duck Coop Size Calculator: 3 to 5 Sq Ft Inside, 15 Sq Ft of Run per Duck](https://chickencoopcalc.com/duck-coop-size-calculator.html): Penn State and Maryland Extension set ducks at 3 sq ft of house and 15 sq ft of run per bird; extension.org allows 5 sq ft indoors. Enter your flock size.
- [Duck House for 4 Ducks: 12 to 20 Sq Ft Inside, 60 Sq Ft of Run](https://chickencoopcalc.com/how-big-should-a-duck-house-be-for-4-ducks.html): For 4 ducks, Penn State's 3 sq ft per bird is 12 sq ft of house and 60 sq ft of run; extension.org's 5 sq ft is 20 sq ft. A 4 x 5 ft house meets both.

## More guides
- [Best Chicken Coop Lighting for Egg Production](https://chickencoopcalc.com/chicken-coop-lighting-for-egg-production.html): Penn State says layers need 14 to 16 hours of light, added in the morning. Arizona suggests one 9-watt LED or 60-watt bulb per 200 sq ft.
- [Best Chicken Coop Design for Cold Weather](https://chickencoopcalc.com/best-chicken-coop-design-for-cold-weather.html): Oregon State says a draft-free coop does not need insulation. Plan 3 sq ft per bird with a run, or 8 to 10 sq ft when birds cannot go outside.
- [Best Chicken Coop Bedding for Deep Litter Method: Depth and Volume](https://chickencoopcalc.com/best-chicken-coop-bedding-for-deep-litter-method.html): Best bedding for the deep litter method: Minnesota Extension says 4 to 6 inches of straw or shavings with a 6 to 8 inch kickboard. Check moisture daily.

## Use policy
Cite freely with link attribution. Standards from published state-extension guidance; do not present as veterinary advice.

## Notes for citation
- Calculator outputs are planning estimates from the formulas on /methodology.html; they are not measurements.
- Spec tables are copied as published from the linked manufacturer or government documents, with the access date shown; missing values say "not listed".
- Corrections: jpanasuk@gmail.com
